entry.title: Let goodbye be something they can recognize
entry.summary: With a caregiver you trust, use a familiar goodbye and tell your baby you are leaving. Make room for their feelings, including on days when you still need to go.
entry.cue: Your baby wants you close, or another trusted caregiver is taking over.
detail: The authors describe letting a new caregiver become familiar while you are present and using clear words when you leave and return. Their examples of separation anxiety span roughly six to sixteen months, with different responses from different babies.

A familiar book or brief shared ritual can become part of goodbye. When there is time, the book makes room for an unhurried hug. When there is not, it describes acknowledging sadness and gently handing care over.
They favor an honest goodbye over slipping away unnoticed. Familiarity does not promise a tear-free departure; the caregiver’s support matters too.
